title: Aircall Pricing 2026: Plans, Add-Ons and Total Cost
summary: Aircall pricing charges per user monthly with 25% off yearly, but seat minimums and hidden fees increase your actual cost. Calculate costs for each plan.
body_markdown:
## Automating Aircall Call Data with Activepieces


### What automation can and cannot do


**Do not expect Activepieces to make Aircall cheaper** .


Its free plan costs $0 and covers the after-call chores, such as CRM logging, missed-call alerts and ticket creation, but only on Aircall plans that expose the events or API it needs, so you can't use it unless you already have a compatible plan.


Pricing your own call volume, as above, comes first. This is the question you ask once you have a plan in mind.


To an accountant it is simple. Every call ends with a small piece of admin: someone logs it, someone chases the missed ones, someone opens a ticket. That work costs agent minutes whether or not anyone counts them.


Once a workflow tool turns it into a trigger and a few actions, the same ending happens without a person doing it. It trims labour, not your phone bill, and it never lowers the per-seat or add-on charges you already face.


### The plan gate that decides whether the workflow runs


A gate in front asks whether your plan exposes the event or API at all. Flows themselves are unlimited on every Activepieces plan, free included, so the three branches don't need three subscriptions' worth of headroom.


If the gate is open, the run is the meter on Activepieces: one credit per run, not per step, so the three-branch flow costs the same as a lone CRM-logging flow.


Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so on their pricing pages the same flow costs more with every action added, which penalises splitting work into smaller stages; here the free plan's 1,000 credits a month count runs only.


It's easy to miss on a pricing page, but that gate is the limit. Whether webhooks or API access come with your plan is something to confirm in Aircall's own documentation or with your account contact before you build anything.


If a plan withholds them, you may be paying for an upgrade just to make the automation possible. Put that upgrade in the cost comparison alongside seats and add-ons.


### Other limits to count before you build


Two more limits are worth stating plainly. Activepieces reacts to events Aircall sends, and it can't recover data Aircall never exposes, however many of its 750 integrations sit downstream of the call.


Each flow run also draws on a credit allowance on the automation side, so a busy line multiplies runs: the free plan's 1,000 credits a month cover 1,000 plain runs, Plus at $20 a month includes 10,000, and anything over costs $0.007 a credit.


Count that against your own call volume before assuming the flow is free.


What follows from this is a short checklist: confirm the event access, count the runs, then price the whole stack.
